description: Ping quality over one hour of monitor data (docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md #5). Rows are per-minute aggregates: target, sent, lost, optional jitter (ms). Targets starting with tcp_ or http_ are TCP/HTTP probes; 'router' is the gateway; anything else is an Internet ping target. Thresholds: >= 60 samples per ping target, >= 20 per probe.

cases.name: no data at all
too few samples: 59 pings, 19 probe rounds
everything clean
router loses 2% (warn)
router loses 5% (bad)
Internet ping loses 5% but probes are clean: ICMP rate-limited
Internet ping and the best probe lose 4%: ISP/WAN
Internet ping loses 2%, no probe data: ping only
high jitter on the Internet only, no probes
high jitter on the router
one probe target blocks port 443, another is clean
probes only, ping blocked entirely (fewer than 60 pings)
rows of one target summed across minutes
boundary: router loses exactly 1% (ok)
boundary: router loses exactly 3% (warn, not bad)
boundary: router loses 3.5% (bad)
boundary: jitter exactly 30 ms is not high
boundary: best probe loses exactly 1% still counts as working
boundary: exactly 60 pings and 20 probe rounds are enough
jitter averaging exactly 30 ms (needs an exact sum, as statistics.fmean) is not high
probes lose 1.5% while ping is clean
